notes: v2.139 (2026-11-26, evening run): 138th tower 'Cornucopia' (a wide red fruit mouth tapering to a curled blue tip — a horn-of-plenty silhouette to demolish, 34 blocks, 4 clusters sizes 12/9/8/5, all 4 colours, no singletons, 0 canonical duplicates) plus a NEW 130th co-play prompt (fill a horn of plenty together — put a big soft toy fruit or pom-pom in a basket or paper cone saying 'in it goes!', name each one — 'apple!… banana!' — count them one, two, three!, then take them out saying 'thank you!' and serve them to your toys; pretend fruit only, big soft toys or pom-poms, nothing small enough to pop in a mouth, a grown-up holds any real fruit). First fresh subject after the pair-completion series ended with Cocoa (v2.138) — Thanksgiving Day, so the harvest horn is the timely pick. Cornucopia research: pretend food play is symbolic play — one object stands for another, the precursor to reading (I'm the Chef Too); serving roles practice empathy and caretaking, sequencing ('first fill, then count, then serve') and naming foods build vocabulary; dropping pieces in and counting 1-2-3 is early math, and playdough-style squeezing/rolling builds the hand muscles later used for writing (CDC tip via Learnings Academy).
